t: Thức giả định & cấu trúc trang trọng
th: Sau **suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose** và **It is essential / vital / important that**, dùng **động từ nguyên mẫu cho mọi ngôi**: I suggest that he **be** present. It is vital that she **arrive** on time. (Anh–Anh hay dùng should + V.)

After **suggest, recommend, insist, demand, propose** and **It is essential / vital / important that**, use the **base form for every person**: I suggest that he **be** present. It is vital that she **arrive** on time. (British English often uses should + V.)
**were to + V**: giả định trang trọng, khó xảy ra: If the government **were to** raise taxes, …
**were to + V**: formal, unlikely hypothesis: If the government **were to** raise taxes, …
Đảo ngữ thay if: **Should** you need help, contact us. (= If you should need) **Were** I in your position, I'd resign. (= If I were)
Inversion instead of if: **Should** you need help, contact us. **Were** I in your position, I'd resign.
Cụm cố định: **Be that as it may** (dù vậy), **Come what may** (dù thế nào), **so be it** (đành vậy).
Fixed phrases: **Be that as it may**, **Come what may**, **so be it**.
ex: The doctor recommended that he ___ smoking.
It is essential that every student ___ the form.
___ you require further information, please contact us.
___ I in your position, I would accept the offer.
If the CEO were to resign, …
They insisted that the meeting ___ postponed.
Should you have any questions please let me know
Nếu có câu hỏi, xin hãy báo tôi.
It is vital that she be informed immediately.

warm.s: The committee has recommended that every applicant submit two references, and it is essential that both be received before the end of March.
q: Theo hội đồng, điều gì là bắt buộc?
What is essential according to the committee?
o: Cả hai thư giới thiệu đến trước cuối tháng Ba
Both references arrive before the end of March
Ứng viên chỉ cần nộp một thư
Ứng viên phỏng vấn vào tháng Ba
Applicants attend an interview in March
e: Thức giả định: recommended that every applicant submit (không thêm -s); it is essential that both be received (dùng be cho mọi ngôi).
Subjunctive: recommended that every applicant submit (no -s); it is essential that both be received (be for every person).
f: it is essential that both be received

warm.s: Should you require any further assistance during your stay, please do not hesitate to contact the reception desk at any time.
e: Should you require = If you require (đảo ngữ trang trọng). Chú ý chính tả assistance và hesitate.
Should you require = If you require (formal inversion). Watch the spelling of assistance and hesitate.
f: Should you require any further assistance

warm.s: Were the government to raise fuel taxes again next year, the cost of public transport would almost certainly rise as well.
e: Were … to + V là giả định trang trọng; nhấn Were ở đầu câu và hạ giọng ở cuối “as well”.
Were … to + V is a formal hypothesis; stress Were at the start and fall at the end on “as well”.

rd2.tx:
Dear Applicant,
Thank you for your application to the Master's programme in Applied Linguistics. The admissions committee has reviewed your file and is pleased to offer you a conditional place for the coming academic year. It is essential that you submit an official IELTS certificate showing an overall score of at least 7.0 no later than 30 June. The committee further recommends that all international students arrive at least one week before the start of term, so that they may attend the orientation programme. Should you be unable to meet the deadline, you are requested to inform the office in writing, stating the reason for the delay. Were the certificate not to reach us in time, we would regrettably be obliged to offer your place to another candidate. We are aware that preparing for an examination of this kind is demanding; be that as it may, the requirement cannot be waived. We look forward to welcoming you in September.
Yours faithfully,
Admissions Office
rd2.tr:
Kính gửi Ứng viên,
Cảm ơn bạn đã nộp hồ sơ vào chương trình Thạc sĩ Ngôn ngữ học Ứng dụng. Hội đồng tuyển sinh đã xem xét hồ sơ và vui mừng cấp cho bạn một suất học có điều kiện cho năm học tới. Bạn bắt buộc phải nộp chứng chỉ IELTS chính thức với điểm tổng tối thiểu 7.0 chậm nhất vào ngày 30 tháng 6. Hội đồng cũng khuyến nghị tất cả sinh viên quốc tế đến trước ngày khai giảng ít nhất một tuần để có thể tham dự chương trình định hướng. Trong trường hợp không kịp hạn, bạn được yêu cầu thông báo bằng văn bản cho văn phòng, nêu rõ lý do chậm trễ. Nếu chứng chỉ không đến kịp, rất tiếc chúng tôi buộc phải trao suất học cho ứng viên khác. Chúng tôi hiểu rằng việc chuẩn bị cho một kỳ thi như vậy rất vất vả; dù vậy, yêu cầu này không thể được miễn. Chúng tôi mong được đón bạn vào tháng Chín.
Trân trọng,
Văn phòng Tuyển sinh

q: Ứng viên phải nộp gì và hạn chót là khi nào?
What must the applicant submit, and by when?
o: Chứng chỉ IELTS từ 7.0 trở lên, chậm nhất 30/6
An IELTS certificate of at least 7.0 by 30 June
Hai thư giới thiệu trước tháng Chín
Bài luận trước buổi định hướng
e: “It is essential that you submit an official IELTS certificate … no later than 30 June” – submit ở dạng giả định sau It is essential that.
“It is essential that you submit an official IELTS certificate … no later than 30 June” – submit is subjunctive after It is essential that.
f: It is essential that you submit an official IELTS certificate

q: Nếu không kịp hạn, ứng viên cần làm gì?
What should applicants do if they cannot meet the deadline?
o: Thông báo bằng văn bản và nêu lý do
Inform the office in writing, giving the reason
e: “Should you be unable to meet the deadline, you are requested to inform the office in writing, stating the reason” – Should you… = If you…
“Should you be unable to meet the deadline, you are requested to inform the office in writing, stating the reason” – Should you… = If you…
f: you are requested to inform the office in writing

q: Cụm “be that as it may” trong thư có ý gì?
What does “be that as it may” signal in the letter?
o: Dù việc ôn thi vất vả, yêu cầu vẫn không được miễn
Although the exam is demanding, the rule still applies
Yêu cầu có thể được miễn
e: Be that as it may = dù vậy đi nữa: thừa nhận ý trước (kỳ thi vất vả) nhưng vẫn giữ quan điểm (yêu cầu không thể miễn).
Be that as it may = even so: it accepts the previous point (the exam is demanding) but keeps the position (the requirement cannot be waived).
f: be that as it may, the requirement cannot be waived

ex2.s: The union has demanded that the management ___ the new shift system immediately and consult the workers before making any further changes.
e: Sau demand that dùng thức giả định: động từ nguyên mẫu cho mọi ngôi (withdraw), kể cả khi chủ ngữ số ít. Chú ý động từ thứ hai consult cũng ở dạng nguyên mẫu.
After demand that, use the subjunctive: the base form for every person (withdraw), even with a singular subject. Note that the second verb consult is also in the base form.

ex2.s: ___ you wish to cancel your subscription at any point, simply send us an email and we will process your request within three working days.
a: Should
e: Đảo ngữ Should + S + V = If + S + (should) V, rất hay dùng trong thư trang trọng, điều khoản dịch vụ. Không dùng Would hay Had ở đây.
The inversion Should + subject + V = If + subject + (should) V, common in formal letters and terms of service. Would or Had don't work here.

ex2.s: It is vital that every passenger keeps their boarding pass until they have left the arrivals hall, as random checks may be carried out.
a: It is vital that every passenger keep their boarding pass until they have left the arrivals hall, as random checks may be carried out.
It is vital that every passenger should keep their boarding pass until they have left the arrivals hall, as random checks may be carried out.
e: Sau It is vital that dùng thức giả định: keep (không -s), hoặc should keep theo kiểu Anh–Anh. “keeps” là dạng thường gặp trong văn nói Anh nhưng không chuẩn ở văn phong trang trọng.
After It is vital that, use the subjunctive keep (no -s), or should keep in British style. “keeps” is heard in informal British English but is not standard in formal writing.

q: Viết lại bằng đảo ngữ, bỏ “if” (bắt đầu bằng “Were…”)
Rewrite with inversion, dropping “if” (start with “Were…”)
ex2.s: If the company were to relocate its headquarters to Singapore, hundreds of employees in Hanoi would lose their jobs.
a: Were the company to relocate its headquarters to Singapore, hundreds of employees in Hanoi would lose their jobs.
e: If + S + were to + V → Were + S + to + V. Giữ nguyên to relocate; mệnh đề chính không đổi.
If + subject + were to + V → Were + subject + to + V. Keep to relocate; the main clause doesn't change.

ex2.s: Ban giám đốc đề xuất rằng cuộc họp được hoãn sang tuần sau để mọi phòng ban có đủ thời gian chuẩn bị số liệu.
a: The board proposed that the meeting be postponed until next week so that every department would have enough time to prepare its figures.
The board of directors proposed that the meeting be postponed until the following week so that all departments have enough time to prepare the data.
The board suggested that the meeting be postponed to next week so that every department has enough time to prepare its figures.
The board proposed that the meeting should be postponed until next week so that every department could have enough time to prepare the figures.
e: propose / suggest that + chủ ngữ + be + V3 (thức giả định bị động): the meeting be postponed. Không viết “is postponed” trong văn phong trang trọng.
propose / suggest that + subject + be + past participle (passive subjunctive): the meeting be postponed. Avoid “is postponed” in formal style.

ex2.s: Come what may,|we are determined|to open|the new library|before the start|of the academic year|in September.
m: Dù có chuyện gì xảy ra, chúng tôi vẫn quyết tâm khai trương thư viện mới trước khi năm học bắt đầu vào tháng Chín.
Come what may, we are determined to open the new library before the start of the academic year in September.
e: Come what may (dù chuyện gì xảy ra) là cụm giả định cố định, luôn tách khỏi câu bằng dấu phẩy và thường đứng đầu câu.
Come what may (whatever happens) is a fixed subjunctive phrase, set off by a comma and usually placed first.

t: Văn phong học thuật: hedging & collocation
th: **Hedging** giảm mức khẳng định, thể hiện thái độ thận trọng: It could be argued that…, The data suggest that…, This may indicate…, … tends to …, … appears to …
**Hedging** softens claims to show academic caution: It could be argued that…, The data suggest that…, This may indicate…, … tends to …, … appears to …
Trạng từ thận trọng: arguably, presumably, relatively, to some extent, in most cases, largely.
Cautious adverbs: arguably, presumably, relatively, to some extent, in most cases, largely.
Collocation chuẩn: **conduct** research, **draw** a conclusion, **raise** a question, **pose** a threat, **play** a crucial role, **a growing body** of evidence.
Standard collocations: **conduct** research, **draw** a conclusion, **raise** a question, **pose** a threat, **play** a crucial role, **a growing body** of evidence.
Tránh khẳng định tuyệt đối khi bằng chứng chưa đủ: “This proves…” → “This provides strong evidence that…”
Avoid absolute claims without full evidence: “This proves…” → “This provides strong evidence that…”
ex: The results ___ that sleep improves memory.
It is too early to ___ a conclusion.
Plastic waste ___ a serious threat to marine life.
Which sentence is the most hedged?
Social media may contribute to depression in some users.
Teachers play a ___ role in motivating students.
It could be argued that technology has made us less patient
Có thể cho rằng công nghệ đã khiến chúng ta kém kiên nhẫn hơn.
This appears to be the most likely explanation.

warm.s: The findings appear to suggest that regular exercise may slow cognitive decline, although further research is needed to confirm this link.
q: Các nhà nghiên cứu tự tin đến mức nào?
How confident are the researchers?
o: Thận trọng, cần thêm nghiên cứu
Không tìm thấy mối liên hệ nào
They found no link at all
e: Ba lớp hedging: appear to, suggest, may – cộng với “further research is needed”. Kết quả có ý nghĩa nhưng chưa được khẳng định chắc chắn.
Three layers of hedging: appear to, suggest, may – plus “further research is needed”. The result matters but isn't presented as certain.

warm.s: A growing body of evidence indicates that air pollution poses a serious threat to the health of young children in urban areas.
e: Collocation chuẩn: a growing body of evidence, pose a serious threat to. evidence không đếm được nên đi với indicates (số ít).
Standard collocations: a growing body of evidence, pose a serious threat to. evidence is uncountable, and a body takes singular indicates.

warm.s: It could be argued that social media has, to some extent, changed the way younger generations form and maintain friendships.
e: Ngắt hơi ở hai dấu phẩy quanh “to some extent”; nhấn ARgued và main-TAIN.
Pause at the commas around “to some extent”; stress AR-gued and main-TAIN.

rd2.tx:
Abstract
This study set out to investigate whether short daily vocabulary reviews lead to better long-term retention than longer weekly sessions among adult learners of English. We conducted a twelve-week experiment with 120 university students in Ho Chi Minh City, who were randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups spent the same total time studying, but one reviewed for ten minutes a day, while the other studied for seventy minutes once a week. The results appear to indicate that daily review is associated with higher scores on a delayed test, although the difference was relatively modest. It should be noted that the sample was limited to a single institution and that participants' motivation was not directly measured. Consequently, the findings cannot necessarily be generalised to other contexts. Nevertheless, they are broadly consistent with a growing body of evidence on the spacing effect, and they raise the question of whether course timetables ought to be redesigned. Further research is needed to establish whether the effect persists over longer periods.
rd2.tr:
Tóm tắt
Nghiên cứu này nhằm tìm hiểu liệu việc ôn từ vựng ngắn hằng ngày có giúp ghi nhớ lâu dài tốt hơn các buổi học dài hằng tuần ở người lớn học tiếng Anh hay không. Chúng tôi tiến hành một thí nghiệm kéo dài mười hai tuần với 120 sinh viên đại học tại TP. Hồ Chí Minh, được phân ngẫu nhiên vào một trong hai nhóm. Cả hai nhóm dành tổng thời gian học như nhau, nhưng một nhóm ôn mười phút mỗi ngày, còn nhóm kia học bảy mươi phút mỗi tuần một lần. Kết quả dường như cho thấy việc ôn hằng ngày gắn với điểm cao hơn trong bài kiểm tra muộn, dù chênh lệch tương đối khiêm tốn. Cần lưu ý rằng mẫu nghiên cứu chỉ giới hạn trong một cơ sở đào tạo và động lực của người tham gia không được đo trực tiếp. Do đó, kết quả chưa hẳn đã khái quát hóa được cho các bối cảnh khác. Tuy vậy, chúng nhìn chung phù hợp với ngày càng nhiều bằng chứng về hiệu ứng giãn cách, và đặt ra câu hỏi liệu thời khóa biểu các khóa học có nên được thiết kế lại. Cần thêm nghiên cứu để xác định hiệu ứng này có duy trì trong thời gian dài hơn hay không.

q: Thời gian học của hai nhóm được phân bổ thế nào?
How was study time arranged for the two groups?
o: Tổng thời gian bằng nhau: 10 phút/ngày so với 70 phút/tuần
Same total: 10 minutes daily vs 70 minutes weekly
Nhóm hằng ngày học nhiều giờ hơn
The daily group studied for more hours
Nhóm hằng tuần học hai buổi mỗi tuần
The weekly group studied twice a week
e: “Both groups spent the same total time studying, but one reviewed for ten minutes a day, while the other studied for seventy minutes once a week.” 10 × 7 = 70, nên tổng thời gian bằng nhau.
“Both groups spent the same total time studying, but one reviewed for ten minutes a day, while the other studied for seventy minutes once a week.” 10 × 7 = 70, so the totals match.
f: Both groups spent the same total time studying

q: Vì sao kết quả chưa chắc khái quát được cho bối cảnh khác?
Why can't the findings necessarily be generalised?
o: Mẫu chỉ ở một trường và động lực không được đo
The sample came from one institution and motivation wasn't measured
Người tham gia không phải sinh viên
e: “It should be noted that the sample was limited to a single institution and that participants' motivation was not directly measured. Consequently…” – hai hạn chế dẫn đến kết luận thận trọng.
“It should be noted that the sample was limited to a single institution and that participants' motivation was not directly measured. Consequently…” – two limitations lead to the cautious conclusion.
f: the sample was limited to a single institution

q: Chênh lệch điểm giữa hai nhóm lớn đến đâu?
How big was the difference between the groups?
e: “although the difference was relatively modest” – relatively là trạng từ hedging, giảm mức độ khẳng định của kết quả.
“although the difference was relatively modest” – relatively is a hedging adverb that softens the claim.

ex2.s: Before any firm conclusions can be ___, the experiment will need to be repeated with a much larger and more diverse sample of participants.
e: Collocation chuẩn là draw a conclusion → conclusions can be drawn. “make / take a conclusion” là lỗi dịch từ tiếng Việt “đưa ra / rút ra kết luận”.
The standard collocation is draw a conclusion → conclusions can be drawn. “make / take a conclusion” are translation errors.

ex2.s: Rising sea levels ___ a serious threat to low-lying coastal areas, including large parts of the Mekong Delta, according to most climate scientists.
a: pose
present
e: Collocation: pose a threat (hoặc present a threat). Chủ ngữ số nhiều (sea levels) nên không thêm -s. Không dùng make / do a threat.
Collocation: pose a threat (or present a threat). The subject is plural (sea levels), so no -s. Don't say make / do a threat.

ex2.s: This experiment proves that bilingual children are more creative than monolingual ones, although only forty pupils from one school took part.
a: This experiment suggests that bilingual children are more creative than monolingual ones, although only forty pupils from one school took part.
This experiment indicates that bilingual children are more creative than monolingual ones, although only forty pupils from one school took part.
e: Với mẫu nhỏ (40 học sinh, một trường), “proves” là khẳng định quá mức. Văn học thuật cần hedging: suggests hoặc indicates.
With a small sample (40 pupils, one school), “proves” overstates the claim. Academic writing needs hedging: suggests or indicates.

q: Viết lại cho thận trọng hơn, bắt đầu bằng “It could be argued that…”
Hedge the claim, starting with “It could be argued that…”
ex2.s: Online learning is less effective than face-to-face teaching for students who struggle to manage their own time.
a: It could be argued that online learning is less effective than face-to-face teaching for students who struggle to manage their own time.
It could be argued that online learning may be less effective than face-to-face teaching for students who struggle to manage their own time.
e: “It could be argued that…” biến một khẳng định tuyệt đối thành một quan điểm có thể tranh luận; phần còn lại giữ nguyên.
“It could be argued that…” turns an absolute claim into an arguable position; the rest stays the same.

ex2.s: Các nhà nghiên cứu đã tiến hành một cuộc khảo sát trên hơn hai nghìn hộ gia đình để tìm hiểu thói quen chi tiêu của họ trong thời kỳ lạm phát cao.
a: The researchers conducted a survey of more than two thousand households to investigate their spending habits during the period of high inflation.
The researchers carried out a survey of over 2,000 households in order to examine their spending habits during a period of high inflation.
The researchers conducted a survey of more than 2,000 households to explore their spending habits during a period of high inflation.
e: “tiến hành khảo sát” → conduct / carry out a survey (không dùng make / do a survey trong văn học thuật). “trên … hộ” → a survey of … households.
“tiến hành khảo sát” → conduct / carry out a survey (avoid make / do in academic writing). “a survey of … households”.

ex2.s: Teachers|arguably play|a crucial role|in shaping|students' attitudes|towards learning,|particularly|in the early years|of primary school.
m: Có thể nói giáo viên đóng vai trò then chốt trong việc hình thành thái độ học tập của học sinh, đặc biệt là trong những năm đầu tiểu học.
Teachers arguably play a crucial role in shaping students' attitudes towards learning, particularly in the early years of primary school.
e: Collocation play a crucial role in + V-ing; trạng từ hedging arguably đứng trước động từ chính.
The collocation play a crucial role in + -ing; the hedging adverb arguably goes before the main verb.

t: Tư duy phản biện & tranh luận
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Rào đón & nhượng bộ (hedging & concession)**
• Nhượng bộ trước khi phản bác: **Admittedly / Granted,** the sample was large, **but**… / **While it may be true that** X, **it does not follow that** Y.
• **Be that as it may,** … (= dù vậy, trang trọng) / **albeit** + tính từ/cụm từ: a useful, **albeit** small, study.
• Rào đón để nghe khách quan: **It may simply be that…**, **seem to have + V3** (The authors **seem to have cherry-picked** the data), **arguably**, **to some extent**.
• Phản bác lịch sự: **I'm not sure that follows.** / **That's quite a leap.** (ngụ ý: kết luận thiếu căn cứ).

**Grammar 1 – Hedging & concession**
• Concede before countering: **Admittedly / Granted,** the sample was large, **but**… / **While it may be true that** X, **it does not follow that** Y.
• **Be that as it may,** … (= even so, formal) / **albeit** + adjective/phrase: a useful, **albeit** small, study.
• Hedge to sound objective: **It may simply be that…**, **seem to have + past participle** (The authors **seem to have cherry-picked** the data), **arguably**, **to some extent**.
• Polite rebuttal: **I'm not sure that follows.** / **That's quite a leap.** (implied: the conclusion isn't justified).

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Câu chẻ để nhấn mạnh**
• **What** + mệnh đề + **is/was** …: **What** the study actually shows **is** a correlation.
• **It is/was** X **that/who** …: **It's** the headline, not the study, **that** misleads readers.
• **It's not** X **so much as** Y: **It's not** the researchers we should doubt **so much as** the reporting.
• **All** + mệnh đề + **is**…: **All** I'm saying **is** that we need more evidence.

**Grammar 2 – Cleft sentences for emphasis**
• **What** + clause + **is/was** …: **What** the study actually shows **is** a correlation.
• **It is/was** X **that/who** …: **It's** the headline, not the study, **that** misleads readers.
• **It's not** X **so much as** Y: **It's not** the researchers we should doubt **so much as** the reporting.
• **All** + clause + **is**…: **All** I'm saying **is** that we need more evidence.

**Ngụy biện & từ gần nghĩa**
• **correlation ≠ causation** (tương quan ≠ nhân quả); **cherry-pick** (chọn lọc dữ liệu có lợi); **straw man** (bóp méo lập luận đối phương rồi bác bỏ); **false dilemma** (đưa ra chỉ 2 lựa chọn); **red herring** (chi tiết đánh lạc hướng); **ad hominem** (công kích cá nhân).
• **imply** (người nói ngụ ý) ↔ **infer** (người nghe suy ra).
• **sceptical** (hoài nghi, cần bằng chứng) ↔ **cynical** (cho rằng ai cũng vụ lợi).
• **refute** (chứng minh là sai) ↔ **deny** (nói là không đúng) ↔ **rebut** (phản bác).
• **evidence** (bằng chứng, không đếm được) ↔ **proof** (chứng cứ xác thực).

**Fallacies & near-synonyms**
• **correlation ≠ causation**; **cherry-pick** (select only helpful data); **straw man** (distort an argument and attack that); **false dilemma** (only two options offered); **red herring** (a distraction); **ad hominem** (attacking the person).
• **imply** (the speaker suggests) ↔ **infer** (the listener concludes).
• **sceptical** (doubtful, wants evidence) ↔ **cynical** (believes everyone is selfish).
• **refute** (prove wrong) ↔ **deny** (say it's untrue) ↔ **rebut** (argue against).
• **evidence** (uncountable) ↔ **proof** (conclusive evidence).

**Phát âm – Ngữ điệu bày tỏ dè dặt**
• Giọng xuống-lên (fall-rise) ↘↗ thể hiện “đồng ý nhưng còn dè dặt”: Well… ↘↗**PART**ly. / In the **SHORT** term ↘↗, perhaps.
• Nhấn tương phản trong câu chẻ: It's the **HEAD**line, not the **STUD**y, that misleads.
• Từ dễ đọc sai: sceptical /ˈskep.tɪ.kəl/, hypothesis /haɪˈpɑː.θə.sɪs/, causation /kɑːˈzeɪ.ʃən/, fallacy /ˈfæl.ə.si/.

**Pronunciation – Intonation for reservations**
• A fall-rise ↘↗ means “I agree, with reservations”: Well… ↘↗**PART**ly. / In the **SHORT** term ↘↗, perhaps.
• Contrastive stress in clefts: It's the **HEAD**line, not the **STUD**y, that misleads.
• Tricky words: sceptical /ˈskep.tɪ.kəl/, hypothesis /haɪˈpɑː.θə.sɪs/, causation /kɑːˈzeɪ.ʃən/, fallacy /ˈfæl.ə.si/.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (30 phút): xem 1 cuộc tranh luận có phản biện (debate club, chương trình truyền hình), ghi lại 5 câu nhượng bộ & 3 ngụy biện bạn nhận ra.
• Nói (30 phút): chọn 1 tiêu đề báo giật gân, nói 2 phút “đóng vai phản biện” (devil's advocate) rồi 2 phút phản bác lại chính mình.
• Đọc (30 phút): đọc 1 bài báo khoa học phổ thông và đối chiếu tiêu đề với nghiên cứu gốc – ghi những chỗ bị phóng đại.
• Viết (40 phút): viết bài phản hồi 150–200 từ đánh giá một luận điểm, dùng ít nhất 2 câu chẻ và 3 cụm rào đón.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học các cặp imply/infer, sceptical/cynical, refute/deny, evidence/proof.

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (30 min): watch a debate (debate club or TV show) and note 5 concessions and 3 fallacies you spot.
• Speaking (30 min): take a sensational headline, play devil's advocate for 2 minutes, then rebut yourself for 2 minutes.
• Reading (30 min): read a popular science article and compare the headline with the original study – note any exaggeration.
• Writing (40 min): write a 150–200-word response evaluating a claim, using at least 2 cleft sentences and 3 hedges.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn the pairs imply/infer, sceptical/cynical, refute/deny, evidence/proof.

rd2.tx:
Tutor: So, the article claims that students who drink coffee get higher grades. Convinced?
Linh: Not entirely. Admittedly, the sample was large, but what the study actually shows is a correlation, not a cause. It may simply be that more ambitious students both study late and drink more coffee.
Sam: I'll play devil's advocate. Granted, correlation isn't causation – but caffeine does improve concentration, doesn't it?
Linh: In the short term, perhaps. Be that as it may, the authors seem to have cherry-picked their data: they ignored the students who dropped out.
Tutor: That's a fair point. And look at the headline: “Coffee makes you smarter.” That's quite a leap from “is associated with”.
Sam: True, though isn't dismissing the whole study because of one headline a bit of a straw man?
Tutor: Good – that's exactly the kind of challenge I want. It's not the researchers we should be sceptical of so much as the way their findings were reported. Before we jump to conclusions, let's look at the methodology.
rd2.tr:
Giảng viên: Vậy bài báo khẳng định sinh viên uống cà phê đạt điểm cao hơn. Các em có bị thuyết phục không?
Linh: Không hoàn toàn ạ. Phải thừa nhận là mẫu nghiên cứu lớn, nhưng điều nghiên cứu thực sự cho thấy là một mối tương quan, không phải nguyên nhân. Có thể đơn giản là những sinh viên tham vọng hơn vừa học khuya vừa uống nhiều cà phê hơn.
Sam: Em xin đóng vai phản biện. Cứ cho là tương quan không phải nhân quả – nhưng caffeine đúng là giúp tập trung hơn, phải không?
Linh: Trong ngắn hạn thì có thể. Dù vậy, các tác giả dường như đã chọn lọc dữ liệu có lợi: họ bỏ qua những sinh viên đã bỏ học.
Giảng viên: Ý đó hợp lý. Và hãy nhìn tiêu đề: “Cà phê làm bạn thông minh hơn.” Đó là một bước nhảy khá xa so với “có liên quan đến”.
Sam: Đúng ạ, nhưng gạt bỏ cả nghiên cứu chỉ vì một tiêu đề chẳng phải là hơi bóp méo vấn đề sao?
Giảng viên: Tốt – đó chính là kiểu chất vấn thầy muốn. Điều chúng ta nên hoài nghi không hẳn là các nhà nghiên cứu mà là cách kết quả của họ được đưa tin. Trước khi vội kết luận, hãy xem xét phương pháp nghiên cứu.

a: Just because crime rose after the new mayor took office doesn't mean his policies caused it; you're confusing correlation with causation and jumping to conclusions.

The minister flatly rejected the allegations at the press conference, but he offered no evidence whatsoever to show that they were untrue.

**refute** = PROVE wrong (with evidence) – which contradicts “offered no evidence”. Simply saying it's untrue → **deny**.

Granted, the sample was quite large, but all it actually shows is a correlation, not a causal relationship.
Admittedly, the sample was quite large, but what it actually shows is just a correlation, not causation.
e: “Phải thừa nhận là” = **Admittedly / Granted**; “điều mà nó thực sự cho thấy là” = câu chẻ **what it actually shows is**.

Before jumping to conclusions, we should consider whether the authors cherry-picked the data that supported their hypothesis.

Before we jump to conclusions, we should look at whether the authors have cherry-picked data to support their hypothesis.

a: It is the headline, not the study itself, that misleads readers.
It's the headline, not the study itself, that misleads readers.
It is the headline that misleads readers, not the study itself.
It is not the study itself but the headline that misleads readers.
e: Câu chẻ **It is X that + V**: đặt thành phần cần nhấn (the headline) giữa “It is” và “that”; động từ chia theo X.
Cleft **It is X that + verb**: put the emphasised part (the headline) between “It is” and “that”; the verb agrees with X.

m: Dù có thể đúng là chính sách mới đã giảm chi phí, điều đó không có nghĩa là nó đã cải thiện chất lượng chăm sóc bệnh nhân.
While it may be true that the new policy has reduced costs, it does not follow that it has improved the quality of care for patients.
e: Khung lập luận kinh điển: **While it may be true that X, it does not follow that Y** – nhượng bộ rồi chỉ ra lỗi suy luận.
A classic frame: **While it may be true that X, it does not follow that Y** – concede, then expose the faulty reasoning.

q: Viết đoạn phản hồi (150–180 từ) đánh giá tiêu đề: “Người chơi game giỏi toán hơn.” Nhượng bộ ít nhất 1 điểm, chỉ ra ít nhất 2 vấn đề về lập luận/bằng chứng, dùng câu chẻ và rào đón.

Write a response (150–180 words) evaluating the headline “Gamers are better at maths.” Concede at least one point, identify at least two problems with the reasoning or evidence, and use clefts and hedges.
ex2.m: At first glance, the headline “Gamers are better at maths” sounds convincing, and admittedly, the survey behind it involved more than five thousand teenagers. Be that as it may, what the data actually shows is a correlation, not a cause. It may simply be that students who are already confident with numbers are drawn to strategy games, rather than the games making them better at maths. What concerns me more is that the survey relied on self-reported grades, which are notoriously unreliable. The researchers also seem to have focused only on puzzle and strategy games, so it does not follow that all gaming has the same effect. To be fair, it is not the study itself that is the main problem so much as the way it has been summarised. Before we jump to conclusions, we would need a controlled experiment comparing similar students over time.
e: Cần có: 1 câu nhượng bộ (admittedly / granted / be that as it may); ≥ 2 vấn đề (tương quan ≠ nhân quả, dữ liệu tự khai, chọn lọc…); ≥ 2 câu chẻ (What… is / It is… that); ≥ 2 cụm rào đón (may simply be, seem to have); đề xuất cách kiểm chứng.

Include: a concession (admittedly / granted / be that as it may); ≥ 2 problems (correlation vs causation, self-reported data, cherry-picking…); ≥ 2 clefts (What… is / It is… that); ≥ 2 hedges (may simply be, seem to have); a suggestion for testing the claim.

t: Ngôn ngữ, dịch thuật & giao tiếp liên văn hoá
th:
**Ngữ pháp 1 – Nói giảm, nói tránh & lịch sự gián tiếp**
• Lùi thì để lịch sự hơn: **I was wondering if** you could… / **I wanted to** ask…
• Thêm từ làm mềm: **just, a bit, possibly, at all**: Would it be **at all** possible to…?
• Câu hỏi phủ định để gợi ý: **Wouldn't it be** better to…? / **Would it be worth** + V-ing…?
• Nói giảm kiểu Anh (understatement): “quite interesting” / “I'll bear it in mind” thường = không mặn mà; “not bad” có thể = khá tốt.
• Giữ thể diện (face): nhận lỗi về mình thay vì chỉ trích: **I may not have made myself clear** (thay cho “You misunderstood”).

**Grammar 1 – Softening & indirect politeness**
• Past forms for politeness: **I was wondering if** you could… / **I wanted to** ask…
• Softeners: **just, a bit, possibly, at all**: Would it be **at all** possible to…?
• Negative questions to suggest: **Wouldn't it be** better to…? / **Would it be worth** + -ing…?
• British understatement: “quite interesting” / “I'll bear it in mind” often = not keen; “not bad” can = quite good.
• Saving face: take the blame yourself instead of criticising: **I may not have made myself clear** (instead of “You misunderstood”).

**Ngữ pháp 2 – Đảo ngữ & đưa thành phần lên đầu để nhấn mạnh**
• Điều kiện đảo ngữ: **Had we spelt** things out (= If we had…), **Were it not for**…, **Should you need**…
• Trạng từ phủ định/hạn chế lên đầu: **Rarely does** a dictionary help… / **Only later did** I realise…
• **Such was** + danh từ + **that**…: **Such was** the confusion **that** we had to start again.
• Cặp gần nghĩa: **translate** (văn bản viết) ↔ **interpret** (dịch nói; cũng = diễn giải); **literal** ↔ **figurative**; **accent** (giọng) ↔ **dialect** (phương ngữ); **fluent** ↔ **proficient** (thành thạo, trang trọng).

**Grammar 2 – Inversion & fronting for emphasis**
• Inverted conditionals: **Had we spelt** things out (= If we had…), **Were it not for**…, **Should you need**…
• Negative/limiting adverbs first: **Rarely does** a dictionary help… / **Only later did** I realise…
• **Such was** + noun + **that**…: **Such was** the confusion **that** we had to start again.
• Near-synonyms: **translate** (written) ↔ **interpret** (spoken; also = understand in a certain way); **literal** ↔ **figurative**; **accent** ↔ **dialect**; **fluent** ↔ **proficient** (more formal).

**Phát âm – Ngữ điệu quyết định thái độ**
• Giọng đều đều (flat) với người bản ngữ có thể nghe như chán hoặc khó chịu: “Fine.” ↘ (lạnh lùng) ↔ “Fine!” ↗↘ (vui vẻ).
• Lời đề nghị lịch sự cần độ lên xuống rõ: I was **WON**dering if you could ↗ possibly…
• Người Việt hay nuốt phụ âm cuối – trong giao tiếp quốc tế hãy giữ rõ: thank**s**, ask**ed**, cultur**e**.
• in**TER**pret /ɪnˈtɝː.prɪt/, **NU**ance /ˈnuː.ɑːns/, **ID**iom, **CON**text.

**Pronunciation – Intonation shapes attitude**
• A flat tone can sound bored or annoyed to native speakers: “Fine.” ↘ (cold) ↔ “Fine!” ↗↘ (warm).
• Polite requests need a clear rise and fall: I was **WON**dering if you could ↗ possibly…
• Vietnamese speakers often drop final consonants – keep them clear internationally: thank**s**, ask**ed**, cultur**e**.
• in**TER**pret /ɪnˈtɝː.prɪt/, **NU**ance /ˈnuː.ɑːns/, **ID**iom, **CON**text.

**Tự luyện ngoài app**
• Nghe (30 phút): xem 1 cảnh phim/series Anh và 1 cảnh phim Mỹ; ghi lại các câu nói giảm và ý thật đằng sau.
• Nói (30 phút): nói cùng một yêu cầu ở 3 mức: thân mật – trung tính – rất trang trọng; ghi âm và so sánh ngữ điệu.
• Đọc (30 phút): so sánh 1 đoạn văn với 2 bản dịch khác nhau; ghi chỗ nào dịch sát nghĩa đen, chỗ nào dịch ý.
• Viết (40 phút): viết email 150–180 từ gỡ rối một hiểu lầm văn hoá một cách tế nhị.
• Từ vựng (15 phút): học 15 thành ngữ về giao tiếp (read between the lines, get the wrong end of the stick, take sth at face value…).

**Practice outside the app**
• Listening (30 min): watch one British and one American TV scene; note the understatements and their real meaning.
• Speaking (30 min): make the same request at 3 levels: informal – neutral – very formal; record and compare your intonation.
• Reading (30 min): compare a passage with two different translations; note where they are literal and where they translate the meaning.
• Writing (40 min): write a 150–180-word email tactfully clearing up a cultural misunderstanding.
• Vocabulary (15 min): learn 15 idioms about communication (read between the lines, get the wrong end of the stick, take something at face value…).

Hi Duc,

Hannah

rd.tx: It has become something of a cliché to claim that failure is the best teacher. Like most clichés, it contains a grain of truth wrapped in a good deal of wishful thinking. Failure is instructive only when it is examined; left unexamined, it tends merely to breed anxiety or, worse, a comfortable story about bad luck. The learner who fails an exam and immediately books another attempt, without asking which questions went wrong and why, has gained little but a receipt. By contrast, the learner who keeps a careful record of errors, revisits them at intervals and deliberately seeks out the kind of task that exposed the weakness is, in effect, turning a setback into a syllabus. Seen in this light, the value of failure lies not in the event itself but in the discipline with which we respond to it.

Thất bại chỉ có ích khi được mổ xẻ; nếu bỏ mặc, nó thường chỉ sinh ra lo âu, hoặc tệ hơn, một câu chuyện dễ chịu về vận rủi. Người thi trượt rồi lập tức đăng ký thi lại mà không hỏi câu nào sai và vì sao thì gần như chẳng thu được gì ngoài một tờ biên lai. e: Cấu trúc “lies not in X but in Y”: giá trị không nằm ở X (the event itself) mà ở Y (the discipline…).
The structure “lies not in X but in Y”: the value isn't in X (the event itself) but in Y (the discipline…).
f: lies not in the event itself but in the discipline

warm.s: Like most clichés, the idea that failure is the best teacher contains a grain of truth wrapped in a good deal of wishful thinking.
e: Chú ý dấu trên clichés và các cụm cố định: a grain of truth, a good deal of, wishful thinking.
Note the accent in clichés and the fixed phrases: a grain of truth, a good deal of, wishful thinking.

warm.s: Left unexamined, a disappointing result tends merely to breed anxiety or, worse, a comfortable story about bad luck.
e: Ngắt hơi sau “Left unexamined” và quanh “worse”; nhấn MERE-ly và BREED.
Pause after “Left unexamined” and around “worse”; stress MERE-ly and BREED.

ex2.s: ___ unexamined, even a painful setback teaches us very little, because we simply move on without asking which decisions led to it.
e: Phân từ quá khứ mang nghĩa bị động: thất bại “bị bỏ mặc” → Left unexamined. “Leaving” sẽ có nghĩa là chính thất bại bỏ mặc cái gì đó – sai logic.
A past participle with passive meaning: the setback “is left” unexamined → Left unexamined. “Leaving” would mean the setback itself leaves something – illogical.

ex2.s: The learner who keeps a careful record of errors and revisits them at intervals is, in ___, turning a setback into a syllabus.
a: effect
e: Cụm cố định in effect = thực chất, trên thực tế. Bẫy chính tả: không viết “in affect”.
The fixed phrase in effect = in reality, essentially. Spelling trap: not “in affect”.

ex2.s: It has become something of cliché to claim that every successful entrepreneur must first go bankrupt at least once before achieving anything.
a: It has become something of a cliché to claim that every successful entrepreneur must first go bankrupt at least once before achieving anything.
e: Cụm cố định là “something of a + danh từ” (khá giống một …): something of a cliché. Thiếu mạo từ a là lỗi rất dễ mắc.
The fixed phrase is “something of a + noun” (rather like a …): something of a cliché. Missing the article a is an easy mistake.

q: Viết lại câu dùng cấu trúc “lies not in … but in …”
Rewrite the sentence using “lies not in … but in …”
ex2.s: What makes a good teacher valuable is not the amount of knowledge they have but their ability to explain it clearly to beginners.
a: The value of a good teacher lies not in the amount of knowledge they have but in their ability to explain it clearly to beginners.
A good teacher's value lies not in the amount of knowledge they have but in their ability to explain it clearly to beginners.
e: Danh hóa “What makes … valuable” thành The value of…, rồi dùng “lies not in X but in Y”. Nhớ lặp lại in trước vế thứ hai.
Nominalise “What makes … valuable” as The value of…, then use “lies not in X but in Y”. Remember to repeat in before the second part.
f: lies not in the amount of knowledge they have but in

ex2.s: Ngược lại, người học chủ động tìm đúng loại bài tập đã làm lộ điểm yếu của mình thì thực chất đang biến thất bại thành giáo trình.
a: By contrast, the learner who deliberately seeks out the kind of task that exposed their weakness is, in effect, turning a setback into a syllabus.
By contrast, a learner who actively looks for the type of exercise that exposed their weakness is in effect turning a setback into a syllabus.
In contrast, the learner who deliberately seeks out the kind of task that revealed their weakness is, in effect, turning failure into a syllabus.
e: “Ngược lại” → By contrast / In contrast; “thực chất” → in effect. Mệnh đề quan hệ who … làm chủ ngữ dài, động từ chính là “is turning”.
“By contrast / In contrast” for the opposite case; “in effect” for “essentially”. The who-clause forms a long subject; the main verb is “is turning”.
f: in effect, turning a setback into a syllabus

ex2.s: The student|who fails an exam|and immediately|books another attempt|without asking|what went wrong|has gained little|but a receipt.
m: Người thi trượt rồi lập tức đăng ký thi lại mà không hỏi mình sai ở đâu thì gần như chẳng thu được gì ngoài một tờ biên lai.
The student who fails an exam and immediately books another attempt without asking what went wrong has gained little but a receipt.
e: Chủ ngữ rất dài (The student who … went wrong) trước động từ chính has gained. “little but” = hầu như không gì ngoài.
A very long subject (The student who … went wrong) before the main verb has gained. “little but” = almost nothing except.
f: has gained little but a receipt
